execution.ref: claude/noop-capability-audit from origin/main 2f1862bed (NOOP-CAPABILITY-AUDIT-01, approved by the Test Lead)
execution.description: Investigated why two run-5 battery DeepONet recipes that differed only by "capacity_fade_head": true rebuilt the same parameters and byte-identical predictions, then added a standing CPU audit: every rebuildable capability of every registered construction contract must change the rebuild identity and the trained-parameter digest of a small fit, or be refused with a typed code.

expected: A supplied construction field changes what Carbon rebuilds, so two recipes that differ by a field are two models.
observed: capacity_fade_head was never dropped: its registered default is true, so the second recipe restated the default and both compiled to the same settings. The two run-5 DeepONet variants were the same model, and any comparison between them compared a model with itself. Their recipe digests still differed, through the strategy hash, so only identity by rebuilt artifact (OWNER-GRAPHITE-TEST-WAVE-04 section 1) counted them as one construction. The new audit found one real no-op: KNN's params_sha256 digests only the stored TRAIN targets, so the neighbour count changes predictions but not the trained-parameter digest. Every other battery, cold-plate and motor capability changed the trained artifact; Burgers (retired) changed its compiled profile for every field.
keep: Before reading two recipes as two variants, compare their compiled settings, not their text: a field restated at its default is the same recipe.
Count and deduplicate constructions by the rebuilt artifact, never by the recipe digest, which changes with any restatement.
Hold the no-op rule with a registry-driven audit that fails when a new contract or capability lands without an effect on the trained parameters.
change: When a session proposes a variant, show the miner or agent which supplied fields equal their defaults, so a restated default is not mistaken for a design change.
Give non-parametric families a trained-state digest that binds their hyperparameters (KNN's neighbour count), versioned so recorded params_sha256 values keep their meaning.
